checked_claims: Puccini composed the 1896 Turin La Bohème; Illica and Giacosa wrote its libretto from Henri Murger's work.
The work is in four scenes/four acts and premiered at Turin's Teatro Regio on 1 February 1896.
Puccini and Ruggero Leoncavallo both worked on the same source subject; the article explicitly identifies Puccini's work.
The Puccini Museum supports the removed courtyard act in Rue Labruyère.
items.distractor_review: Verdi, Rossini, and Wagner did not compose Puccini's La Bohème. The bare title remains a wording backlog because Leoncavallo also set the subject, but he is not an offered option and the revised article makes the distinction explicit.

items.source_limits: The public stem's title alone does not distinguish Puccini's work from Leoncavallo's same-subject opera. The options nevertheless contain one correct answer; qualification should be tracked as a future wording improvement.

checked_claims: Puccini composed Madama Butterfly; Illica and Giacosa wrote its libretto, with Long and Belasco in the source chain.
The La Scala premiere was on 17 February 1904, and the setting and named characters are supported by the archive and libretto.
The 1904 Milan version is two acts and the 1906 Paris version is three acts; Rome's archive entry is separately labelled three acts.
The article treats Nagasaki as the setting of a fictional drama and avoids exoticising claims.
items.distractor_review: Verdi, Rossini, and Bizet did not compose Madama Butterfly; the direct composer wording has one best offered answer.
